I don't know how to say it in French.

original: 何て言えばいいか分からないよ。

en.text: I don't know what to say.

original: 彼は何も言わずに立ち去った。

en.text: He went away without saying a word.

original: 脳震盪だとお医者さんに言われました。

en.text: The doctor told me I had a concussion.

original: 何とも言い難いな。

en.text: That's hard to say.

original: 彼女は何も言わず出ていった。

en.text: She went out without saying a word.

original: 何回言わせる気？

en.text: How many times do I have to tell you?

original: 二酸化炭素は炭酸ガスとも言います。

en.text: Carbon dioxide is also called carbonic gas.

original: 親に向かってその言いぐさは何だ！

en.text: How dare you talk to your parents that way!

original: 彼女が何と言おうと、信じません。

en.text: Whatever she says, I don't believe her.

original: こんな下手な言いわけ初めて見た。

en.text: I've never seen this shoddy of an excuse in my life.

original: 何も言わず、行って下さい。

en.text: Go without saying anything.

original: フランス語で話すと、子供っぽいって言われるんだよな。

en.text: I've been told that I sound like a kid when I speak French.
When I speak French, people say I sound like a kid.

original: 何回も何回も言わせんなよ。

en.text: Don't make me say it again and again.

original: 相手は何も言わずに電話を切ったんだ。

en.text: The caller hung up without saying anything.

original: ここ浄閑寺、通称「投げ込み寺」の墓地には、最後の休息場所を見つけた何千もの遊女、いわゆる「楽しみのための女性」の慰霊碑があり、それは言い知れない哀愁に満ちていて、どういうわけか何度でもここに戻ってきたい気持ちが沸き起こる。

en.text: Here at the Jokanji, also known as the "Nagekomi-dera", in the cemetery there is a memorial to thousands of prostitutes, the so-called "women of pleasure", who have found their final resting place here. It's filled with an indescribable melancholy, and, for some reason, it makes me want to come back here again and again.

original: 陰口を言われるのは誰だって嫌さ。

en.text: No one likes to be talked about behind their back.

original: 互いに自分の預金高は言い合わなかった。

en.text: They did not tell each other about the size of their savings.

indices: 互い に 自分 の 預金 高(たか) は 言い合う[01]{言い合わなかった}~

original: もっと水を飲んだ方がいいと先生に言われたよ。

en.text: My doctor told me that I should drink more water.
My doctor told me I should drink more water.

original: その答えは、何かを達成できることなど冷笑し、恐れ、疑えとあまりにも長い間、多くの人から言われ続けてきた人々を、歴史の円弧に手をかけて向きを変え、もう一度、より良い明日のための希望へと導くものだ。

en.text: The answer is to guide those, who have been told for too long and from too many to sneer at, fear, and doubt that anything can be accomplished, to change the direction of history and once more hope for a better tomorrow.
